units.title: Unity in Diversity
units.intro: Grammar: active and passive (2): the present and past continuous and the present and past perfect passive.

lessons.title: Passive in continuous and perfect tenses

cards.title: Passive in continuous and perfect tenses
rule: **Present continuous passive:** am/is/are + **being** + past participle: *The road **is being repaired**.*
**Past continuous passive:** was/were + **being** + pp: *The hall **was being cleaned** when we arrived.*
**Present perfect passive:** has/have + **been** + pp: *The results **have been published**.* **Past perfect passive:** had + **been** + pp: *The tickets **had been sold** before we came.*

examples.text: A new school is being built in our village.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **BeING for continuING; BeEN for perfect (havE BEEN).**

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Continuous passives add being (is/was being + pp); perfect passives add been (has/have/had been + pp). The tense of the active sentence stays the same in the passive.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Haile should have sold the car after possessing it for ten years. (Choose the appropriate passive voice)

options.A: The car should have been sold after been possessed by Haile for ten years.
options.B: After being possessed for ten years, the car should be sold by Haile.
options.C: The car should have been sold after being possessed by Haile for ten years.
options.D: The car should have been sold after being possessed for Haile for ten years.
options.E: The car shall be sold after being possessed by Haile for ten years.

cards.why: The active structure 'should have sold' (modal + have + V3) becomes 'should have been sold' in passive. 'Possessing it' (gerund) becomes 'being possessed' (passive gerund).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The rare African manuscript ________ from the national archives before the guards noticed the broken window.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Two past actions: first the manuscript was stolen, then the guards noticed.

**Step 2:** The earlier action takes the past perfect; the manuscript did not steal → passive.

**Step 3:** had been + past participle → **had been stolen**.

**Tip:** The subject does not do the action → passive: the right form of be + past participle (is done, was done, is being done, has been done, will have been done).

**In Tigrinya:** እዚ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክልተ ኣብ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ዝተፈጸሙ ድርጊታት የነጻጽር። እቲ ጽሑፍ ዝተሰረቐሉ ግዜ፡ እቶም ሓለውቲ ቅድሚ ምርኣዮም ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ካብቲ ሓደ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ንላዕሊ ዝቐደመ (earlier past) እዩ። ስለዚ ሕሉፍ ፍጹም ጥንሳዊ መዋቕር (past perfect passive) 'had been stolen' (Option B) ክንጥቀም ኣለና።

cards.title: Step by step: present continuous passive
cards.problem: Complete: "A lot of money ____ currently ____ (raise) to build the new library."

steps.text: **Step 1: Who does the action?** People raise the money; the money does not raise anything → **passive**.
**Step 2: Find the tense.** *currently* = now → present continuous.
**Step 3: Make the passive.** is/are + **being** + past participle → *money* is singular → **is being raised**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The national examination papers ________ by next Friday afternoon, according to the official schedule.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Papers cannot print themselves → **passive**.

**Step 2:** *by next Friday* = finished before a future time → future perfect.

**Step 3:** Future perfect passive: will have **been** + past participle → **will have been printed**.

**Tip:** The subject does not do the action → passive: the right form of be + past participle (is done, was done, is being done, has been done, will have been done).

**In Tigrinya:** 'By next Friday' (ክሳብ ዝመጽእ ዓርቢ) ዝብል ሓረግ መጻኢ ፍጹም እዋን (Future Perfect) ከም ዘድልየና የረድኣና። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'examination papers' (መፈተኒ ወረቐት) ህይወት ኣልቦ ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ Future Perfect Passive 'will have been printed' (Option B - ተሓቲሙ ክውዳእ እዩ) ክስራዕ ኣለዎ።

cards.title: Present perfect, present perfect continuous and past perfect
rule: **Present perfect** = *have/has + past participle*. Use it for a past action that is important **now**, or with no exact time: *I **have lost** my pen. She **has visited** Axum twice.*
Use **since** + a starting point (*since 2020, since Monday*) and **for** + a length of time (*for three years*): *We **have lived** here **for** ten years.*
**Present perfect continuous** = *have/has + been + -ing*. Use it for an action that started in the past and is **still going on**: *Aster **has been working** here **since** 2019.*
With a **finished time** (*yesterday, last week, ago, in 2015*) use the **past simple**, not the present perfect: *They **finished** the road three weeks ago.*
**Past perfect** = *had + past participle*: the **earlier** of two past actions: *When we arrived, the bus **had left**.*

examples.text: I have finished my homework yesterday.
She has been waiting for an hour.
She is waiting here since 9 o'clock.
examples.fix: She has been waiting here since 9 o'clock.

examples.text: When I got to the station, the train had left.

cards.pattern: have/has + V3  ·  have/has been + V-ing  ·  had + V3

cards.title: Which tense?
head: Time words
Tense
Example
rows: I **have known** her **for** years. It **has been raining** since morning.
before, after, when, by the time (two past actions)
past perfect for the earlier one
The film **had started** when we arrived.

cards.title: Step by step: "since" → present perfect continuous
cards.problem: Complete: "Aster ____ (work) in this laboratory since she finished university five years ago."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time word.** *since she finished university* = from then until **now**.
**Step 2: Is she still working there?** Yes → the action is still going on.
**Step 3: Choose the tense.** still going on + since → present perfect continuous: **has been working** (*has worked* is also possible).
**Watch out:** ✗ *is working since…* – English does not use the present continuous with *since*.

cards.title: Step by step: "ago" → past simple
cards.problem: Complete: "The company ____ (complete) the new road three weeks ago."

steps.text: **Step 1: Find the time word.** *three weeks ago* = a finished time in the past.
**Step 2: Choose the tense.** finished time → past simple.
**Step 3: Answer.** **completed** (✗ *has completed* – the present perfect never goes with *ago*).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** *since 2018* = from 2018 until now.

**Step 2:** From the past until now → present perfect: **have lived**.

**Step 3:** *live / are living* are present only; *lived* is finished past.

**Tip:** since / for / already / yet / ever → present perfect (have + V3). Still going on + how long → have been + -ing. ago / yesterday → past simple.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: By the time the ambulance arrived, the injured man ____ to hospital by a taxi driver.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Two past actions: first the man was taken, then the ambulance arrived.

**Step 2:** Earlier action → past perfect; he did not take himself → passive.

**Step 3:** had been + past participle → **had been taken**.

**Tip:** Finished time (yesterday, ago, last…) → past simple. Long action interrupted → was/were + -ing. Earlier of two past actions → had + past participle.

tips.text: **BeING for continuING; BeEN for perfect (havE BEEN).**

games.title: Match the form to its example

questions.q: The bridge ____ at the moment.
questions.label: 1. The bridge ____ at the moment.

similar.q: Change to passive: They are building a clinic.
Change to passive: Someone has stolen my book.

why: Answer B: is being repaired
At the moment = present continuous.
Passive: is being repaired.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.label: 2. All the tickets ____ already.

similar.q: Change to passive: Someone has stolen my book.
Correct: The cake was been eaten.
similar.a: The cake was being eaten (in progress) or The cake had been eaten (finished earlier).

why: Answer B: have been sold
Already = present perfect.
Passive: have been sold.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

similar.a: The cake was being eaten (in progress) or The cake had been eaten (finished earlier).

why: Answer A: was being cleaned
Action in progress at a past moment.
Past continuous passive.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.label: 7. The match ____ (watch) by many people when the lights went o

similar.a: The cake was being eaten (in progress) or The cake had been eaten (finished earlier).

questions.q: By 1991 many towns ____ (destroy) by the war.
questions.label: 8. By 1991 many towns ____ (destroy) by the war.

similar.q: Change to active: The letter had been written by Ruth.

why: An action before a past time (1991) → past perfect passive.
questions.tip: Say the sentence aloud with your answer; it must be grammatical and make sense.

questions.q: The new hospital ____ at the moment.
questions.label: 9. The new hospital ____ at the moment.

similar.q: Complete: The road ____ (repair) now.
Complete: The cars ____ (wash) at the moment.

why: Answer B: is being built
"at the moment" shows an action in progress now.
Present continuous passive: am/is/are + being + past participle.
"is being built".
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: The cultural festival ____ every year since 1992.
questions.label: 10. The cultural festival ____ every year since 1992.

similar.q: Complete: Three new schools ____ (open) this year.
Complete: The letter ____ just ____ (send).

why: Answer B: has been held
"since 1992" with a continuing habit points to the present perfect.
Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle.
"has been held".
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Change to the passive: "They were translating the speech into nine languages."
questions.label: 11. Change to the passive: "They were translating the speech into nine languages."

similar.q: Passive: "They were painting the hall."
Passive: "Someone was watching us."

questions.answer: The speech was being translated into nine languages.
why: The verb is past continuous active (were translating).
Past continuous passive: was/were + being + past participle.
"The speech" is singular → was being translated.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the past perfect passive?
questions.label: 12. Which sentence is in the past perfect passive?

similar.q: Make past perfect passive: The tickets (sell) before we arrived.
similar.a: The tickets had been sold before we arrived.

similar.q: Complete: By 1995 the bridge ____ (rebuild).

options.A: The food had been prepared before the guests arrived.
options.B: The food was prepared before the guests arrived.

why: Answer A: The food had been prepared before the guests arrived.
Past perfect passive: had + been + past participle.
Only "had been prepared" matches.
The others are past simple, present perfect and present continuous passives.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Eritrea has nine ethnic groups. Which word best describes a country with many cultures?
questions.label: 13. Eritrea has nine ethnic groups. Which word best describes a country with many cultures?

similar.q: Noun from "diverse".
Meaning of "unity".

why: Answer A: diverse
"diverse" means made up of many different kinds.
"identical" means exactly the same; "divided" suggests conflict.
So "diverse" fits.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Correct the error: "The traditional dances have been perform at the festival."
questions.label: 14. Correct the error: "The traditional dances have been perform at the festival."

similar.q: Correct: The rooms are being clean.
Correct: The work had been finish.

questions.answer: The traditional dances have been performed at the festival.
why: The perfect passive needs the past participle after "been".
"perform" → "performed".
So: have been performed.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Read: "In Asmara you can hear Tigrinya, Tigre, Arabic and other languages in the same market. People from different groups share holidays and help one another at weddings and funerals." What is the main idea?
questions.label: 15. Read: "In Asmara you can hear Tigrinya, Tigre, Arabic and other languages in the same market.…

similar.q: Find a detail showing cooperation.
similar.a: People help one another at weddings and funerals.

similar.q: Which word shows variety in the passage?

options.A: Weddings are more important than funerals.
options.B: Only one language is spoken in Asmara.
options.D: Different groups live together in harmony.

why: Answer D: Different groups live together in harmony.
The passage mentions many languages in one market.
It also shows groups sharing holidays and helping one another.
These details support unity in diversity.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: "Many songs ____ in nine languages since independence."
questions.label: 16. Choose the correct form: "Many songs ____ in nine languages since independence."

similar.q: Complete: The museum ____ (visit) by thousands since 2000.
Complete: Many trees ____ (plant) since last year.

why: Answer A: have been recorded
"since independence" points to the present perfect.
Songs are recorded by people, so use the passive.
have + been + past participle → have been recorded.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Which sentence is NOT passive?
questions.label: 17. Which sentence is NOT passive?

similar.q: Active or passive: "The book was written in 1990."
Active or passive: "She has written a book."

options.A: A new road has been built.
options.B: The workers are building a new road.
options.D: A new road is being built.

why: Answer B: The workers are building a new road.
In the passive, the subject receives the action and the verb is be + past participle.
In "The workers are building a new road", the workers do the action: active.
The other three are passive.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Choose the best expression to show respect for another culture.
questions.label: 18. Choose the best expression to show respect for another culture.

similar.q: Polite question about a festival.
similar.a: "Could you tell me what this festival celebrates?"

similar.q: Word for respecting others' beliefs.

options.A: I'd love to learn more about your traditions.
options.B: Our culture is better than yours.
options.C: I don't care about your customs.

why: Answer A: I'd love to learn more about your traditions.
Showing respect means being interested and polite.
The first option shows interest.
The others are judgemental or rude.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: The results ____ when the principal came into the hall.
questions.label: 19. The results ____ when the principal came into the hall.

similar.q: Complete: The house ____ (paint) when we arrived.
Complete: The patients ____ (examine) when the power failed.

why: Answer A: were being announced
The announcement was in progress when the principal came in.
Past continuous passive: was/were + being + past participle.
"were being announced".
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Which word means "to live together peacefully"?
questions.label: 20. Which word means "to live together peacefully"?

similar.q: Noun from "coexist".
Word meaning "a shared feeling of belonging".

why: Answer D: coexist
The prefix co- means together; "exist" means live.
"coexist" = live together, usually peacefully.
The others suggest rivalry or division.
questions.tip: Passive = the right form of "be" + past participle. Continuous uses being; perfect uses been.

questions.q: Have you ____ been to Keren?

similar.q: Complete: "I ____ (know) him since 2015."
Complete: "She ____ (leave) an hour ago."

why: Answer A: ever
*ever* is used in present perfect questions about experience.
*ago* and *yesterday* go with the past simple.
questions.tip: since / for / already / yet / ever → present perfect (have + V3). Still going on + how long → have been + -ing. ago / yesterday → past simple.

questions.q: My uncle ____ in Massawa for twenty years. He still lives there.

similar.q: Complete: "I ____ (know) him since 2015."
Complete: "She ____ (leave) an hour ago."

why: Answer B: has lived
*for twenty years* + he still lives there → from the past until now.
Present perfect: **has lived**.
questions.tip: since / for / already / yet / ever → present perfect (have + V3). Still going on + how long → have been + -ing. ago / yesterday → past simple.

questions.q: They ____ the match two days ago.

similar.q: Complete: "I ____ (know) him since 2015."
Complete: "She ____ (leave) an hour ago."

why: Answer B: won
*two days ago* = finished time → past simple: **won**.
questions.tip: since / for / already / yet / ever → present perfect (have + V3). Still going on + how long → have been + -ing. ago / yesterday → past simple.

questions.q: I am tired because I ____ (study) since 6 o'clock.

similar.q: Complete: "I ____ (know) him since 2015."
Complete: "She ____ (leave) an hour ago."

why: *since 6 o'clock* and I am still tired now → the action has been going on until now.
Present perfect continuous: **have been studying**.
questions.tip: since / for / already / yet / ever → present perfect (have + V3). Still going on + how long → have been + -ing. ago / yesterday → past simple.

questions.q: When we got to the cinema, the film ____ (already / start).

similar.q: Complete: "I ____ (know) him since 2015."
Complete: "She ____ (leave) an hour ago."

why: Two past actions: the film started first.
Earlier action → past perfect: **had already started**.
questions.tip: Finished time (yesterday, ago, last…) → past simple. Long action interrupted → was/were + -ing. Earlier of two past actions → had + past participle.

questions.q: Correct the error: "She has finished her project last week."

similar.q: Complete: "I ____ (know) him since 2015."
Complete: "She ____ (leave) an hour ago."

accept: She finished her project last week
questions.answer: She finished her project last week.
why: *last week* is a finished time.
Finished time → past simple: *finished*.
questions.tip: since / for / already / yet / ever → present perfect (have + V3). Still going on + how long → have been + -ing. ago / yesterday → past simple.
